name: Runtime
description: What the host checks before a guest runs, which posture it builds, and how invocations share a process.

scenarios.title: Threads holding their own Sandboxes hold their own guest state
given: two Threads, each with its own Sandbox
one of them having set a guest global
scenarios.when: the other Thread reads that global
scenarios.then: it reads nothing the first Thread set

scenarios.title: Threads sharing one Sandbox still evaluate on their own identity
given: several Threads evaluating on one shared Sandbox, each supplying its own identity for its invocation
scenarios.when: each Thread's guest code resolves the identity it was given

scenarios.title: The entrypoint verb shares a Sandbox the same way
given: several Threads running an entrypoint on one shared Sandbox, each supplying its own identity for its invocation
scenarios.when: each Thread's entrypoint resolves the identity it was given

scenarios.title: Releasing the lock does not pool the Handles
given: several Threads invoking their own Sandboxes constructed with `gvl: :release`
scenarios.when: each Thread restores the Handles its own invocation minted

scenarios.title: Releasing the lock does not cross the Handle arguments either
given: several Threads invoking their own Sandboxes constructed with `gvl: :release`
scenarios.when: each Thread passes its own Handles back as dispatch arguments

scenarios.title: A guest that cannot state its ABI version does not run
given: a Guest Binary exporting no ABI version
scenarios.when: a Sandbox is constructed over it

scenarios.title: A guest stating another ABI version does not run
given: a Guest Binary reporting an ABI version the Host Gem does not implement
scenarios.when: a Sandbox is constructed over it

scenarios.title: A refused artifact is never remembered as usable
given: a Guest Binary already refused once for its ABI version
scenarios.when: a Sandbox is constructed over the same path again

scenarios.title: The strongest posture is the one nobody has to ask for
given: Sandbox options carrying no `profile:`
scenarios.when: the options are read

scenarios.title: Both rungs of the ladder may be requested
given: Sandbox options carrying each ladder rung in turn
scenarios.when: the options are read
scenarios.then: each reports the rung it was given

scenarios.title: A posture off the ladder is not a posture
given: Sandbox options carrying a `profile:` value the ladder does not name
scenarios.when: the options are built

scenarios.title: A runtime that built less than was asked for does not run
given: options requesting a rung
a runtime declaring a rung below it
scenarios.when: the request is enforced as a floor

scenarios.title: A posture nobody can place ranks below every request
given: options requesting any rung
a runtime declaring a posture the ladder does not name
scenarios.when: the request is enforced as a floor

scenarios.title: A stronger posture satisfies a weaker request
given: options requesting a rung
a runtime declaring that rung or a stronger one
scenarios.when: the request is enforced as a floor

scenarios.title: The bundled runtime builds whichever rung is asked for
given: the bundled Guest Binary
scenarios.when: a Sandbox is constructed at each ladder rung in turn
scenarios.then: each construction reports the rung it requested

scenarios.title: The request reaches the runtime and comes back
given: the bundled Guest Binary
scenarios.when: a runtime is built from that path at each ladder rung in turn
scenarios.then: each runtime declares the rung it was built for

scenarios.title: The runtime refuses an unnameable posture on its own
given: the bundled Guest Binary
scenarios.when: a runtime is built from that path with a `profile:` the ladder does not name

scenarios.title: Holding the lock is what happens when nobody chooses
given: Sandbox options carrying no `gvl:`
scenarios.when: the options are read

scenarios.title: Both scheduling modes may be requested
given: Sandbox options carrying each scheduling mode in turn
scenarios.when: the options are read
scenarios.then: each reports the mode it was given

scenarios.title: A mode outside the set is not a mode
given: Sandbox options carrying a `gvl:` value the mode set does not name
scenarios.when: the options are built

scenarios.title: The runtime refuses an unknown mode on its own
given: the bundled Guest Binary
scenarios.when: a runtime is built from that path with a `gvl:` the mode set does not name

scenarios.title: Releasing the lock changes no value
given: one Sandbox under each scheduling mode
scenarios.when: each evaluates the same guest source

scenarios.title: Releasing the lock changes no dispatch result
given: one Sandbox under each scheduling mode, each with the same Service bound
scenarios.when: each evaluates guest source that dispatches to that Service

scenarios.title: The lock is reacquired deep enough for a nested dispatch
given: one Sandbox under each scheduling mode, each with the same yielding Service bound
scenarios.when: each evaluates guest source whose dispatch dispatches again

scenarios.title: Releasing the lock changes no capture
given: one Sandbox under each scheduling mode
scenarios.when: each evaluates guest source that writes to standard output
scenarios.then: both carry the same captured bytes

scenarios.title: Released Sandboxes on distinct Threads each answer their own
given: several Threads, each with its own Sandbox constructed with `gvl: :release`
scenarios.when: every Thread evaluates guest source computing from its own input
scenarios.then: each Thread receives the result of its own input

scenarios.title: A requested posture is honored the same way by either frontend
given: a scenario requesting the hermetic posture explicitly
scenarios.when: both frontends run it

scenarios.title: A posture switch resolves the same way on either frontend
given: a scenario switching to the permissive posture
scenarios.when: both frontends run it
scenarios.then: they resolve it the same way

text: The runtime is what stands between a request and a guest that runs. Three
checks happen before any guest does: the artifact states an ABI version the
host implements, the requested isolation posture is one the ladder names, and
the posture actually built is not weaker than the one accepted.
The scheduling scenarios pair off deliberately. Releasing the lock is a
scheduling change and nothing else, so each witness runs one scenario under
both modes and compares — a value, a dispatch, a nested dispatch, a capture.
The host-parallel run is the one that shows what the mode is for.
The ambient denial the hermetic posture rests on has no scenario of its own:
the default Guest Binary exposes no time or entropy surface for guest code to
read, which is the posture itself, so there is nothing to observe from inside.
